name: Hag, Masca
body:
Masca (Village Hag)
CR 7

This old woman seems pretty ordinary. There’s a gentle smile on her face when she beckons you to come near, but a weird glint in her eye tells you something’s not right.

XP 3,200
CN Medium monstrous humanoid
Init +4; Senses darkvision 60 ft; Perception +16

DEFENSE

AC 20, touch 15, flat-footed 15 (+4 Dex, +1 dodge, +5 natural)
hp 85 (9d10+36)
Fort +6, Ref +10, Will +10
DR 10/cold iron and magic; Immune charm and compulsion effects; SR 18

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee quarterstaff +11/+11/+6/+6 (1d6+3)
Special Attacks knockout gaze (DC 17)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 9th; concentration +12; Intelligence-based)

At will—disguise self
3/day—remove disease
1/day—lesser astral projection, sending

STATISTICS

Str 16, Dex 19, Con 17, Int 17, Wis 18, Cha 14
Base Atk +9; CMB +12; CMD 26
Feats Dodge, Improved Two-Weapon Fighting, Toughness, Two-Weapon Fighting, Weapon Focus (quarterstaff)
Skills Craft +15, Heal +14, Intimidate +14, Perception +16, Sense Motive +13, Spellcraft +12, Use Magic Device +11
Languages Abyssal, Common, Infernal, Sylvan
SQ book of command, change shape (any animal, plant, or object; beast shape II, plant shape I, or object form II)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Book of Command (Su)

Each masca carries a book of command, an occult tome that represents the source of her power. The masca can use her book of command as an occultist’s implement for the Divination school as if she were a 9th-level occultist. A masca is considered to possess a mental focus pool of 10 points for this purpose, plus the danger sight, future gaze, object sight, and watchful eye focus powers. A book of command only works for the masca who owns it and disappears if separated from its owner for more than 24 hours or if the hag dies (unless it is left as a legacy). A masca cannot use her spell-like abilities or change shape without her book of command.

Knockout Gaze (Su)

Once per combat, the masca can attempt a gaze attack against an opponent to knock them out. If the target fails a Fortitude save, they fall unconscious for 1d4 rounds. A successful Fortitude save reduces this effect to staggered for 1 round. The DC of this save is Intelligence-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate plains, fields, and villages
Organization solitary or coven (3 or more)
Treasure standard

Masche are uncharacteristic not-evil hags who live in villages along humans or in isolated shacks in the country. Though capricious and vengeful, they don’t harbor any special desire to harm people. A masca could act as a hamlet’s wise woman, curing diseases and giving advice; indistinguishable from a common woman by day, she will leave her home at night to andare in masca (assume her true identity) and fare la fisica (practice magic), taking other forms and sending her soul to fly very far from her physical body. Masche are jealous of their art and don’t like to be disturbed while practicing it, receiving inappropriate questions about their magic and private life, or being insulted with names as “strega” (witch) or “megera” (hag). A masca will most likely curse someone who is excessively curious or rude. They are also able to see the past and future by browsing their book of command and can warn people about danger or ill-willed spirits in their vicinity, though in doing so they risk being mistaken for the actual source of danger or evil. Country people can live along a masca for years, respecting her and turning to her for help, or can suddenly decide masche are evil and hunt them to burn at the stake, often killing many innocent women in the process.

A masca will most often choose a husband and raise a normal family in a village. According to tradition, masche could be immortal if they didn’t pass their book of command on to a heir, but such a masca would only continue to grow older and frailer without the chance to end her sufferings.

What is certain is that a masca will always ensure to find a worthy successor and transmit the book of command to her before dying. Sometimes the book is replaced by another symbol of power, such as a ball of wool, a broomstick, or a ladle. Typically, the masca’s heir is chosen among her family or descendants, like a daughter or granddaughter, and transforms into a masca when receiving her legacy. A masca could also select a man as her heir, but these masconi are rare and lack the ability to pass their power on in their turn, so a mascone’s power and bloodline finishes with him.

Covens

Masche only form covens with other masche and not with any other types of hags. A masche coven does not gain the animate dead and reincarnate spell-like abilities of typical covens. Instead, the coven gains access to prediction of failure and retrocognitionoa. When all three hags of the coven are within 10 feet of one another, the save DCs of their spell-like abilities increases by 1 for each member of the coven. The save DCs are Intelligence-based.
